bodyMarkdown:
Android Do Not Disturb can quiet workday notifications without silencing everyone. Set its filters to allow calls or messages from the people you choose, keep essential app alerts and alarms available, then schedule the mode around your work hours. The exact controls vary by phone and Android version.

DND is useful when notifications pull your attention away. It does not block an app from opening, so it will not stop a reflexive trip to a social feed. This guide is about setting notification boundaries and keeping the interruptions you still need.

## Choose what should get through

Before changing settings, decide what you need to hear during a work block. That might be calls from family, calendar reminders or one work app. Everything else can wait until the block ends.

On many recent Android phones, open Settings, tap Modes, then Do Not Disturb. Open Notification filters to choose what can interrupt you. Google's [Android Do Not Disturb guide](https://support.google.com/android/answer/9069335?hl=en) lists filters for people, apps, alarms and other interruptions. Menu names and options vary by device. Some of the steps in Google's guide apply only to Android 14 and later.

## Allow calls from the people who matter

In Notification filters, open People and choose which calls and messages can come through. The available options depend on your phone. You may be able to allow all contacts, starred contacts or selected people while DND is on.

Android also has an option for repeat callers. On supported devices, a second call from the same person within 15 minutes can ring through. This can help with urgent calls while keeping most calls quiet. Check the setting on your own phone before relying on it. Google's [instructions for setting notification filters](https://support.google.com/android/answer/9069335?hl=en#zippy=%2Cset-what-to-block-or-who-can-interrupt-you) explain the current controls.

If your phone offers a choice between calls and messages, set each separately. You may want family calls to ring but personal messages to wait. Then ask someone you trust to test the rule before your next important work block.

## Keep essential app alerts and alarms

Use the Apps filter to allow only the apps that need to interrupt you. A calendar or an authenticator may be useful during work. Social, shopping and entertainment alerts usually can wait. If an app has urgent and non-urgent notifications, Android may not let DND separate them. In that case, adjust the app's own notification settings too.

Check Alarms and other interruptions before you start. Decide whether alarms, reminders, calendar events or media should come through. Google notes that some critical system notifications cannot be blocked, even when DND is on.

## Set a time limit or schedule

For a one-off work block, turn on DND from Quick Settings and choose a duration if your phone offers one. Google lists choices such as staying on until you turn it off, running for a set time or asking each time. A timer is handy because it prevents DND from staying on after you finish.

For a repeating workday, create a schedule in the DND settings. Set the days and start and end times you actually need. Do a short test first. A schedule that starts too early or blocks a family call every evening will get switched off.

Phone makers place these controls in different menus. If you cannot find Modes, search Settings for "Do Not Disturb" or check the support page for your phone model.

## Do Not Disturb does not block apps

DND filters notifications. It does not stop you from opening an app or scrolling once you are there. Android's Focus mode can pause selected apps on supported devices, but its break and scheduling options differ from DND. Google's [Digital Wellbeing guide](https://support.google.com/android/answer/9346420?hl=en) describes that separate feature.

If app openings are the problem, notification filters alone will not solve it. CogniFocus includes DND Focus Mode to help silence interruptions during a focus session. Its Distraction Shield blocks selected apps during active sessions. You can use the controls that match the distraction you actually have.

## A simple workday setup

Start with one work block and a small allow list. Let chosen calls and essential alerts through, silence the rest, and set DND to turn off when the block ends. Test the setup once before depending on it.

If you still find yourself opening distracting apps, keep DND for alerts and add a separate app boundary. If the main distraction was the constant buzz, DND may be enough.

[See CogniFocus on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.ionic.cognifocus).
